h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: A parallel conv path into node 3 already supplies conv features, so adding a conv on edge 5 is partly redundant.
A conv on edge 2 gives node 2 rich features, so the conv on edge 5 completes a deep serial conv chain.
With edge 5 removed, node 2 has no route to the output, so changing edge 2 has essentially no effect.
Replacing the valuable input-output skip offsets the conv's gain, unlike replacing none or pooling.
Turning an existing 3x3 conv on edge 3 into a skip loses learned capacity, whereas replacing none or pool adds a useful shortcut.
With edge 1 absent, node 2 depends entirely on node 1, so removing edge 0 cuts both intermediate nodes off and leaves only edge 3.
A sibling conv into node 3 keeps learned features flowing, so a pool on edge 4 is less harmful.
Replacing the key serial conv on edge 2 with parameter-free pooling removes depth, making the edit far more harmful than replacing none or skip.
A backup conv path from node 1 to the output limits the damage from removing edge 5.
Without the direct input-output edge, removing edge 5 can leave the output nearly disconnected, causing a much larger accuracy drop.
